data.narrative:
Deep Fission, founded by Liz and Rich Muller, is a nuclear energy company approaching IPO with $80M raised to date. The valuation exercise drew from a comp universe of 8 peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private firms (X-Energy, Oklo, Valar Atomics, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy), all operating in the frontier nuclear sector.

The peer-median method proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage comparables. Only one IPO-stage peer exists in nuclear energy, falling short of the three-datapoint minimum required for reliable triangulation. Adjacent-stage and similar-valuation-tier filters yielded no additional matches, making an all-sector median inappropriate for a specialized frontier-tech company with distinct risk and unit economics profiles.

This analysis therefore cannot support a specific valuation range without additional applicable methodologies—such as DCF with disclosed revenue and capex assumptions, precedent transaction analysis from recent nuclear energy M&A, or expansion of the comparable set to include adjacent deep-tech infrastructure sectors. Key uncertainties center on regulatory pathway clarity, capital intensity relative to peer profiles, and whether the private peer set reflects sufficient maturity heterogeneity to isolate IPO-stage benchmarks. Further quantitative work is required before recommending a range.
